summary.text: August Pfluger is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 11th District, which he has represented since January 2021.

A U.S. Air Force Academy graduate and former fighter pilot who retired from the Air Force as a colonel in 2026, he chairs the Republican Study Committee and the Homeland Security Committee's Counterterrorism and Intelligence Subcommittee and also sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee, according to his official biography.

paragraphs.text: Pfluger was born in Harris County, Texas, and graduated from Central High School in San Angelo.
His official biography describes him as a seventh-generation Texan who grew up in San Angelo, where he lives with his wife, Camille, and their three daughters.
He earned a bachelor's degree from the United States Air Force Academy and master's degrees from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, Air University and Georgetown University.

Pfluger served in the U.S. Air Force for 26 years as a fighter pilot and squadron commander, flying combat missions in the Middle East, according to his official biography, and retired as a colonel on February 1, 2026; Ballotpedia lists service in the Air Force Reserve.
He also served on the staff of the National Security Council before entering electoral politics.
Pfluger was elected to Congress in 2020 to succeed Rep. Mike Conaway and took office on January 3, 2021.

On the House Energy and Commerce Committee he serves on the subcommittees on Energy, Environment, and Communications and Technology, and he chairs the Homeland Security Committee's Subcommittee on Counterterrorism and Intelligence.
He chairs the Republican Study Committee, the House conservative caucus, and is founder and co-chair of the Congressional Free Enterprise Caucus.

He was elected in 2025 to chair the U.S. Air Force Academy Board of Visitors, having previously been appointed to it by the Speaker of the House, and his office says he received the Congressional Management Foundation's 2025 Democracy Award for constituent correspondence and outreach.
